message.content:
Finding the “best” sushi spot in Los Angeles is a bit of a moving target—taste, service, and even the vibe can change from week to week. Below is a snapshot (as of 2024) of the most highly‑rated sushi restaurants in LA, based on Michelin stars, food‑critic reviews, and community buzz. I’ve grouped them by what makes each one stand out, so you can pick the one that fits your mood.

| Rank | Restaurant | Location | Why It’s a Top Pick | Highlights |
|------|------------|----------|---------------------|------------|
| **1** | **Sushi Gen** | Little Tokyo (Downtown) | 2 Michelin stars; legendary for its omakase and meticulous fish selection. | Omakase tasting menu (≈$200–$250), seasonal sashimi, and a rare “sashimi of the day” that changes daily. |
| **2** | **Sushi Zo** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; known for its minimalist, high‑quality approach and impeccable service. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a small but well‑curated sake list. |
| **3** | **Sushi Tetsu** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a cult favorite for its “sushi of the day” and a relaxed, no‑frills atmosphere. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a focus on the freshest catch. |
| **4** | **Kappo Sato** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a blend of traditional kaiseki and modern sushi techniques. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), seasonal kaiseki courses, and a carefully curated sake list. |
| **5** | **Sushi Nakazawa** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a refined, high‑end experience with a focus on precision and flavor. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a sophisticated setting. |
| **6** | **Sushi Kappo** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a newer addition that’s quickly become a favorite for its creative omakase. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a focus on seasonal ingredients. |
| **7** | **Sushi Saito** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a small, intimate spot that offers a unique omakase experience. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a focus on the freshest fish. |
| **8** | **Sushi Tatsu** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a modern take on sushi with a focus on sustainability. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a focus on sustainable sourcing. |
| **9** | **Sushi Kappo** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a newer addition that’s quickly become a favorite for its creative omakase. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a focus on seasonal ingredients. |
| **10** | **Sushi Tatsu** | West Hollywood | 1 Michelin star; a small, intimate spot that offers a unique omakase experience. | Omakase (≈$200–$250), “sashimi of the day,” and a focus on the freshest fish. |

### How to Choose

| Factor | What to Look For | Recommendation |
|--------|------------------|----------------|
| **Budget** | Omakase menus range from $200–$250 per person. If you’re looking for a more affordable option, consider a “sashimi of the day” lunch or a set menu. | For a splurge, go to Sushi Gen or Sushi Zo. For a mid‑range experience, try Sushi Tetsu or Kappo Sato. |
| **Atmosphere** | Some places are formal (Sushi Gen, Sushi Zo), while others are more relaxed (Sushi Tetsu, Kappo Sato). | If you want a formal, Michelin‑starred experience, choose Sushi Gen or Sushi Zo. If you prefer a laid‑back vibe, go to Sushi Tetsu. |
| **Specialty** | Some restaurants focus on omakase, others on “sashimi of the day.” | If you want a full omakase, pick Sushi Gen or Sushi Zo. If you want a quick, high‑quality lunch, try the “sashimi of the day” at any of the top spots. |
| **Location** | Downtown (Sushi Gen) vs. West Hollywood (most others). | If you’re in Downtown, Sushi Gen is the obvious choice. If you’re in West Hollywood, any of the others will work. |

### Quick Tips

1. **Reservations** – All Michelin‑starred sushi spots require reservations months in advance. Call early or book online.
2. **Dress Code** – Most of these places have a smart‑casual dress code. No flip‑flops or athletic wear.
3. **Sake Pairing** – Many of the top spots offer a curated sake list. Ask for a recommendation if you’re unsure.
4. **Tipping** – A 15–20% tip is customary for omakase experiences.

### Bottom Line

If you’re looking for the pinnacle of sushi in LA, **Sushi Gen** is the clear leader with two Michelin stars and a legendary omakase. For a slightly less formal but equally stellar experience, **Sushi Zo** and **Sushi Tetsu** are top choices. If you’re on a budget or just want a quick, high‑quality lunch, the “sashimi of the day” at any of these spots will satisfy. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
